summary.summary: Cumberland's draft Annual Governance Statement (AGS) 2025/26, presented to Audit and Risk Committee for approval, confirms the council remains under externally-chaired improvement oversight tied to Exceptional Financial Support (EFS): the AGS itself states the council applied for EFS to fund transformation following local government reorganisation (LGR), and establishing an externally chaired Improvement Panel reporting via Audit and Risk Committee was a condition of that application. No EFS amount is given in this document. Beyond the EFS-linked governance arrangements, the AGS flags an ambitious 2026/27 capital programme needing robust monitoring, committee reports routinely landing at or near the statutory deadline (limiting statutory-officer scrutiny time), and a need to continue reviewing the council's wholly owned companies and partnerships. For a lender, this reads as a council still operating inside EFS-conditioned external oversight rather than one that has exited it.

signals.headline: Council applied for Exceptional Financial Support to fund transformation after LGR; an externally chaired Improvement Panel, a condition of that EFS application, continues to meet regularly and report to Audit & Risk Committee as 'a key source of reassurance that the Council is exercising financial control' (Appendix 1 page 8)
signals.why: EFS-conditioned external oversight remaining in place signals the council has not yet demonstrated it can manage its finances without exceptional government support.

news_drafts.headline: Cumberland audit team scraps three reviews as workload squeezes internal checks
news_drafts.lead: Cumberland's internal audit team has cancelled three planned reviews and postponed a fourth because of staffing pressures, the council's Audit and Risk Committee heard this month. The planning service standards audit received only partial assurance, meaning some control objectives are not being met, while the audit of the council's social enterprise returned limited assurance, indicating significant control weaknesses. The team is investigating eight allegations of fraud, theft or wrongdoing, two of which have been referred to police. The audit cancellations mean key areas including demand forecasting in adult social care and a cross-cutting family support programme will not be reviewed this year. The committee also noted that high-priority debt risks have not been formally recorded in the council's risk management system.

findings.headline: Council carrying unquantified Equal Pay claim relating to over 400 employees transferred from former County Council
findings.detail: The council received an Equal Pay claim in August 2023 relating to over 400 employees of the former County Council now employed by Cumberland. The report notes 'the council is carrying risk from an Equal Pay claim' but the financial impact is unquantified.
findings.matters: Equal pay claims can result in substantial backdated pay awards. An unquantified contingent liability is a hidden risk to the budget, particularly if the claim is settled while the council is managing large deficits.
findings.quote: receipt in August 2023 by the council and Westmorland & Furness Council of an Equal Pay claim relating to over 400 employees of the former County Council now employed by the council which the council is taking steps to minimise

findings.headline: General Fund reserves are only just above minimum required; asset sales yield insufficient and behind schedule
findings.detail: General Fund reserves: 31.3.27 estimated at £26.51m (vs £26.15m in 2023). Expected asset sales yields: £1.3m (2025-26), £2.76m (2026-27), £6.07m (2027-28). CIPFA concludes: 'reserves are low and not significantly increasing' and 'asset sales are insufficient to significantly increase reserves.'
findings.matters: Low reserves with no buffer leaves the council vulnerable to any variance in spending or income. Asset sales are the only planned reserve replenishment and they are materializing slowly.
findings.figures: General Fund reserves: £26.51m (near minimum); asset sales: £1.3-6.07m annually planned
findings.quote: Though the council has preserved the overall level of reserves, the general fund is only just above the minimum required and though they are accelerating, asset sales are insufficient to significantly increase reserves.

findings.headline: SEND identified as 'the most significant long-term financial risk' with no fully implemented sufficiency solution
findings.detail: CIPFA notes SEND cost pressures are 'largely outside short-term control' due to EHCP growth, insufficient local provision, and high transport costs. The council remains dependent on external market provision. Costs are likely to continue to increase without accelerated delivery of local provision.
findings.matters: SEND is nationally a growing cost pressure; a council admitting it lacks control suggests this line item will continue to be a budget pressure and potential overspend source.
findings.figures: SEND and inclusion pressures drove Q3 2025-26 children's overspend; 56% of 2026-27 children's budget taken by placements and SEND transport
findings.quote: SEND represents the most significant long-term financial risk to the council.

findings.headline: May 2027 council elections will change leadership at the moment the most difficult budget decisions are required
findings.detail: CIPFA notes: 'whole council elections will take place in May 2027 it is critical that by the end of 2026 there is a credible and costed plan to bridge the budget gaps.' Later: 'the budget gaps for 2028-29 and 2029-30 will require some difficult political choices in a situation where the elections of May 2027 may deliver a new inexperienced leadership for the council.'
findings.matters: Leadership change during fiscal crisis creates risk of policy reversal, delayed decisions, or loss of corporate knowledge at a critical moment.
findings.figures: Elections May 2027; budget decisions needed by end-2026; gaps arise 2028-29 and 2029-30 after changeover
findings.quote: whole council elections will take place in May 2027 it is critical that by the end of 2026 there is a credible and costed plan to bridge the budget gaps detailed in the MTFP for 2027-28

findings.headline: Council has no appetite for the tax increases and service cuts required to close the budget gap for 2028-29 and beyond
findings.detail: The report states: 'the council has no appetite to seek increases in Council Tax above the referendum threshold and there is no plan to cease any discretionary services, which will be needed to close the budget gap for 2028-29.' This gap of £50-60m cannot be filled by savings or asset sales alone without service reductions or tax rises.
findings.matters: Political unwillingness to take difficult decisions, combined with a £50m+ gap, signals the council may face a second or third EFS request rather than solving the problem structurally.
findings.figures: Gap 2028-29: £50.85m; 2029-30: £59.51m; no mechanism identified to bridge these
findings.quote: the council has no appetite to seek increases in Council Tax above the referendum threshold and there is no plan to cease any discretionary services, which will be needed to close the budget gap for 2028-29.
